correctness.rationale: For an exact three-row change, the altered column images are permuted by a derangement of three labels, hence a 3-cycle; the same applies to symbol images since changing the column in a fixed row also changes the symbol. Thus both signs are invariant. A fresh exhaustive replay enumerates every symbol permutation, retains precisely those with bijective induced columns, and generates both candidate column cycles per row triple; neither the generation nor the adjacency step can omit a legal vertex or edge. All-source BFS and edge accounting return class profiles (vertices, edges, diameter) of (486,972,8) for each sign class other than (+,+), and (567,1215,7) for (+,+), one component per class. There are 2025 vertices, 4131 edges, and degree counts {3:486,4:1458,6:27,15:54}. A fresh small-order check generated by row assignments and tested Hamming distance directly on every pair: order 5 has 15 isolates and no edges; order 7 has 133 vertices, 196 edges, a 112-vertex component and 21 isolates. The frozen scripts and recorded outputs were inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: Exact results apply to the labeled fixed square and the specified move. This is a finite exhaustive computation, not a general theorem on larger orders or a formal verification.

value.rationale: Three changed rows are the smallest possible transition between distinct transversals: a two-row column swap could preserve the symbols only if the two row labels were equal. Order nine is the smallest composite odd cyclic order, and the exact component classification decides reachability under this minimal move, not merely a count of vertices. The smaller-order comparison establishes that the parity obstruction need not be the only one; diameters give a concrete bound on within-class navigation at order nine.
residual_risks: No mixing-time conclusion or extension to larger orders is supported.
